sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Tottenham host Brighton at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Tottenham sit 18th on 30 points, while Brighton are on 46 after a strong recent run. The Sofascore model leans towards an away win, with a moderate chance that both teams score.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Tottenham are 1-1-3 across their last 5 in all competitions, failing to score in their last 2 league matches (vs Nottingham Forest, at Sunderland). They conceded 12 in that span. Brighton are 4-0-1 with 3 clean sheets and back-to-back wins away (at Sunderland, at Burnley).

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Brighton are unbeaten in the last 3 meetings, including a 4-1 win in London and a 2-2 draw on the south coast. Both teams have scored in 6 straight head-to-head matches, with a consistent trend towards high-output games.

sections.subtitle: Tactical notes
sections.text: Tottenham press and tackle at a high rate (league-best 19.4 tackles per game) and deliver a steady crossing threat (153 accurate crosses; 11 headed goals). However, they struggle in aerial duels (46.5% won) and have been without a clean sheet for an extended run, with Cristian Romero missing. Brighton’s wide threat and ball carriers (Kaoru Mitoma, Yankuba Minteh) combine with Pascal Groß’s delivery, while Jan Paul van Hecke anchors a disciplined back line.

sections.subtitle: Key players
sections.text: Tottenham: Richarlison (9 goals), Pedro Porro’s supply from the right, Xavi Simons as a creator. Brighton: Danny Welbeck (12 goals), Pascal Groß’s set-piece and passing quality, Minteh’s dribbling threat (stood out in the recent 2-2).

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Stuart Attwell averages 3.5 yellow cards per match. Tottenham commit many fouls (377) and carry a high yellow count (79), pointing to a moderate card profile. Head-to-heads have produced high corner counts and Tottenham average 5.2 corners per game, so corners are likely above average again.

sections.subtitle: Season stats snapshot
sections.text: Tottenham have scored 40 and conceded 51, with 7 clean sheets. They rank well for accurate crosses (153, rank 6) and headed goals (11, rank 3), but lag in aerial duels (46.5%, rank 18). They allow 12.8 opposition shots per game (rank 6), yet errors and big moments have hurt them.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Brighton come in with stronger form and a favourable recent record in this fixture. Tottenham’s crossing and late surges can trouble them, but Brighton’s structure and attacking balance give them the edge. Prediction: Brighton to win, with both teams to score slightly more likely than not.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham and Brighton are level at half-time (1-1). Pedro Porro headed Tottenham in front on 39 minutes and Kaoru Mitoma equalised on 45 minutes. Tottenham have produced the better chances by expected goals despite less possession (Tottenham 0.80, Brighton 0.20; possession 46% vs 54%). Both sides have hit the woodwork once. Brighton have advanced more often into the final third (29 vs 16), but Tottenham have reached the penalty area more frequently (17 vs 14), reflecting a more direct route to goal.

halftimeSections.subtitle: First-half summary
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham’s structure without the ball was solid and they won more duels (55%). Porro was the main outlet on the right and converted his chance. Brighton grew into the match through Pascal Groß’s supply (3 key passes, 1 assist) and Mitoma’s sharp movement, while Danny Welbeck passed up a big chance. Shots on target were level (2-2), but Tottenham’s chances carried greater quality.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham controlled the early stages with a strong spell before the midway point, then surged again approaching the interval, which preceded Porro’s goal. Brighton wrestled momentum from around the 27th minute through to the mid-30s with sustained pressure. After Tottenham’s breakthrough, Brighton finished the half on top, responding in stoppage time to level.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key numbers at half-time
halftimeSections.text: Expected goals: Tottenham 0.80, Brighton 0.20. Shots on target: 2-2. Big chances: Tottenham 2, Brighton 1 (big chances missed 1-1). Corners: Tottenham 5, Brighton 3. Final-third entries: Tottenham 16, Brighton 29. Penalty-area entries: Tottenham 17, Brighton 14. Duels won: Tottenham 55%, Brighton 44%. Aerial duels: Tottenham 42%, Brighton 55%.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical notes and adjustments
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham’s right side is the clearest route, with Porro’s overlaps and early deliveries troubling Brighton’s left. Given Brighton’s edge in aerial duels, Tottenham may profit more from low crosses and cut-backs rather than high crosses. Brighton’s best threat comes from quick switches to isolate Mitoma wide and his inside runs off Groß’s early passes. If Tottenham compress the middle, Brighton can look for underlaps and late arrivals to the edge of the box. Managing transitions will be key: Tottenham should keep a spare defender on Mitoma’s side, while Brighton must close Porro’s channel and defend the second phase after clearances.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Discipline and corners
halftimeSections.text: Cards: Tottenham 1 yellow (Yves Bissouma), Brighton 1 yellow (Mats Wieffer). Corners: Tottenham 5, Brighton 3. The first-half tempo suggests another 1-2 cards after the break and a high total corner count, likely finishing in the 11-14 range, with Tottenham continuing to generate set-piece pressure from the right.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: The pattern points to Tottenham creating the clearer openings, especially down the right, while Brighton remain a threat in transitions through Mitoma. If Tottenham maintain their duel advantage and keep entries into the box high, they are well placed to edge ahead. Brighton’s route back is via quick switches and exploiting the space behind Tottenham’s advancing full-backs.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Tottenham to edge a narrow win. Next goal Tottenham, created down the right. Predicted full-time: Tottenham 2-1 Brighton.
